header.running_head: Rebuking and Advising Caution to those who Do Not Abstain from Worldly Luxuries and Who Indulge themselves

blocks.text: Another narration states that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) said, "Never did three days pass Rasulullaah ﷺ in his entire life without his debts exceeding his dues."[^1]

Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) said, "How far are your lifestyles to that of your Nabi ﷺ! Whereas he was most abstinent from the world, you people are most desirous of it."[^2]
What Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said to his Son who asked him for a New Garment

Hadhrat Maymoon reports that when one of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA)'s sons asked him for new lower garment, claiming that his was torn, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "Cut your garment (off from where it is torn) and then wear the rest." When (he noticed that) the youngster did not like the response, he said, "Shame on you! Do not be one of those people who spend everything that Allaah provides for them on their bellies (on food) and backs (on clothing)."[^3]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)

Hadhrat Thaabit reports that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) who was busy building a house for himself. Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) remarked, "You are loading large boulders on people's necks." Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) explained, "I am having a house built." When Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) repeated his remark, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Dear brother! It appears as if you are upset with me for this." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "Had I passed you when you were tending to the faeces of your family, it would have been more pleasing to me than what I am now seeing."[^4]
What Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said to his Daughter Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) when he saw her Wearing New Clothes

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I once wore a new upper garment of mine and was very taken aback by it as I looked at it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said to me, 'What are you looking at? Allaah is not looking at you (with affection).' 'Why not?' I asked. He replied, 'Don't you know that when self-adoration enters a servant because of worldly beauty, Allaah detests the person until the beauty is lost (and the self-adoration with it).' I then took off the garment and gave it away as Sadaqah. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, 'That shall perhaps atone for you.'"[^5]
Ah, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.1 Pg.315). Ibn Asaakir and Ibn Najjaar have also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.148).
